//: DRAFT — see README.md. For the editor and for `tsc --noEmit` only.
Nothing is ever built from this: plain `node` runs the .ts files directly by stripping types at
load. That is what `erasableSyntaxOnly` enforces — it fails the typecheck on anything node
cannot strip (enum, namespace, parameter properties), so the editor catches it before node does.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` + `noEmit` are the pair that lets the source say `./utils.ts`,
which is what node requires for relative imports and what tsc would otherwise reject.
